messages.subject: using the dredge function with gdistsamp
messages.subject_clean: using the dredge function with gdistsamp
messages.body_plain:
When trying to use the dredge function I am encountering an error that I have been unable to find any documentation on here or elsewhere:

Error in umf_get_specs(x) : unknown "unmarkedFitGDS" model structure

Below is the code for my unmarked frame, global model, and dredge function.

APPA15umf<-unmarkedFrameGDS(y=as.matrix(data[,2:7]),
                         siteCovs=(fin.covs),
                         numPrimary=1,
                         yearlySiteCovs = data.frame(fin.detcovs),
                         dist.breaks=c(0,20,40,60,80,100,120),
                         unitsIn="m", survey="point")

glob.mod<-gdistsamp(~SiteAge+Acres+elev+prism15+sap15+shrb15+forb15+grass15+bare15+RGsm15+RGmd15+RGlg15,~1,~1, data=APPA15umf, output="density", mixture="P")

df<-dredge(glob.mod, beta="none",evaluate="TRUE",rank="AICc",m.lim=c(NA,10))

I have also tried the dredge funciton, eliminating the beta, evaluate, rank, and m.lim arguments with the same result. Any insight as to what might be generating this error would be much appreciated. Additionally, if there is another function that folks might recommend in lieu of the dredge function, please share!

Thank you!

messages.subject_clean: [unmarked] Re: Transect length in gdistsamp and/or survey effort as a yearlySiteCovs
messages.body_plain:
I need to account for variable survey effort during point counts when running distsamp or gdistamp to estimate density. I tried using offset codes like those provided by Mathew and others, but I cannot get anything to run that takes variable effort into account.

For example, though we attempted to visit every point 6 times. There are some points we only surveyed 4 or 5 times for various reasons.

(effort <- data.frame(effort = KEVdf2$SurveyEffort, row.names=KEVdf$UniqueID))
siteCovs(umf)$length=effort
summary(umf)
hn_Null_offset=distsamp(~1~offset(log(length)),umf)

This code adds effort and length to umf, but when I run the model I get this error: Error in model.frame.default(stateformula, siteCovs, na.action = NULL) :
  invalid type (list) for variable 'offset(log(length))'

Any advice on how to account for variable survey effort in point counts is welcome. Thanks.

On Monday, January 14, 2013 at 3:07:23 PM UTC-6, Richard Chandler wrote:
> Hi Matthew,
>
> Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you want a model like:
>
> E[N(i,t)] = M(i)*phi(i,t)*PROP(i,t)
>
> Where PROP(i,t) is the proportion of transect i surveyed on primary period t. I don't think this is possible in unmarked, but you could approximate it by using PROP as a covariate of phi.
>
> Richard
>
>
>
>
> On Mon, Jan 14, 2013 at 12:00 AM, Matthew Butler <wildlif...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Andy, thanks for your quick reply.  My concern is variation in transect length for a site across primary occasions.  For example, site i on occasion 1 might but 100 m, on occasion 2 it might be 100 m, but on occasion 3 it might be 50 m.  The ‘gdistsamp’ function only allows for 1 length for each site.  One could simply average the 3 lengths to account for varying effort across occasions but I am concerned that availability is effected by effort.  Another words, on occasion 3 the availability should be reduced because less effort was applied.  Perhaps I misunderstand what the availability parameter is though.
> >
> >
> >
> > Erik, thanks for suggesting the offset.  The offset feature provides an alternative way to deal with varying transect lengths but gives same result as including correct lengths in the umf (see code below).
> >
> >
> >
> > #-----
> >
> >
> >
> > # Based on the code from the January 2012 Workshop.
> >
> > library(unmarked)
> >
> > source("http://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/webinars/2012-january/data/utils.R?attredirects=0&d=1")
> >
> >
> >
> > # Set-up the data for analysis; simulated data from unmarked.
> >
> > dists=read.csv(system.file("csv","distdata.csv",package="unmarked"))
> >
> > levels(dists$transect)
> >
> > levels(dists$transect)=c(levels(dists$transect),"g")
> >
> > levels(dists$transect)
> >
> >
> >
> > # multinomial format using the formatDistData function.
> >
> > yDat=formatDistData(dists,distCol="distance",
> >
> >                        transectNameCol="transect",dist.breaks=c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20))
> >
> >
> >
> > # Transect-specific covariates:
> >
> > (covs=data.frame(canopyHt=c(5,8,3,2,4,7,5),
> >
> >                     habitat=c('A','A','A','A','B','B','B'),row.names=letters[1:7]))
> >
> >
> >
> > # Mmake an unmarkedFrameDS.
> >
> > umf=unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat),siteCovs=covs,survey="line",
> >
> >                        dist.breaks=c(0,5,10,15,20),tlength=rep(100, 7),
> >
> >                        unitsIn="m")
> >
> >
> >
> > # USE OF OFFSET if units of varying length do this:
> >
> > effort=c(1,1,1,2,2,1,1)
> >
> > siteCovs(umf)$length=effort
> >
> >
> >
> > # Use the offset in the model.
> >
> > hn_Null_offset=distsamp(~1~offset(log(length)),umf)
> >
> >
> >
> > # Replace lengths in umf with lengths adjusted for effort.
> >
> > umf_lengths=unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat),siteCovs=covs,survey="line",
> >
> >                        dist.breaks=c(0,5,10,15,20), tlength=rep(100,7)*effort,
> >
> >                        unitsIn="m")
> >
> >
> >
> > # Run the model on new umf with adjusted lengths.
> >
> > hn_Null_nooffset=distsamp(~1~1,umf_lengths)
> >
> >
> >
> > summary(hn_Null_offset)
> >
> > summary(hn_Null_nooffset)
> >

> > Thanks,

> > On Sunday, January 13, 2013 5:34:57 PM UTC-7, erikw...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Royal discusses an "offset function" for variable line transect lengths in day 2 of their webinar (~1:00:30 into the video).
> > >
> > > http://www.pwrc.usgs.gov/Royalvideo.cfm
> > >
> > > On Sunday, January 13, 2013 1:12:20 PM UTC-6, Matthew Butler wrote:
> > > > It appears that ‘gdistsamp’ assumes site-specific transect length is the same for each survey (correct me if I am wrong). Sometimes survey logistics precludes completion of a site’s transect due to various reasons. For example, an observer during an aerial survey might get air sick and not survey their side of a transect for a while. In ‘distsamp’, I would deal with such a scenario by cutting transect length in half for all the sites in which the observer was not actively surveying. However, in ‘gdistsamp’ it is not so clear what to do. Let’s say a survey has 500, 1000-m transects and 50 of the 500 sites (transects) were only surveyed by 1 observer during 1 of 4 surveys (in the other 3, both observers were active). My first instinct is to make site-specific transect length 875 m ([1000+1000+1000+500]/4) for the 50 sites that were not completely surveyed. However, availability is different at those 50 sites because survey effort differed. Should effort be included as a covariate in the ‘yearlySiteCovs’ to account for that change in availability? Should site-specific transect length be adjusted accordingly?
> > > >
> > > > I think this question would also apply to situations were some sites are not surveyed during some of the primary surveys? For example, 50 of the 500 sites might only be surveyed on 3 of the 4 surveys. Would effort be adjusted to 750 m ([1000+1000+1000+0]/4) for those 50 site that were only surveyed 3 times, should effort be included as a covariate in the ‘yearlySiteCovs’, or both?
> > > >
> > > > Thanks,
> > > >
> > > > Matthew Butler

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: unmarkedMultFrame - problem with yearlySiteCovs
messages.body_plain:
The answer might be "Don't mention it."  The model won't mind.  As the years become farther away from the initial year the predicted occupancy probability will approach a constant no matter what psi1 happens to be.  For the case where the colonization and extinction parameters are constant (gamma and epsilon, respectively), the occupancy probability will approach gamma/(gamma+epsilon).  All of the years will have slightly different occupancy probabilities as they approach this limit.  So you'll still get different estimates for each year.

However, if there really needs to be yearly site covariates, then that's a different problem.

Jim

messages.body_plain:
Hi Richard,

I came across this post while looking for some explanation of why my predicted estimates using gdistsamp() are so unreasonable, and I saw your reply to this post. In my case I visited all my sites 3 times, so my plan was to just use them as extra effort, but while reading through the discussions in the forum I decided that gdistsamp was the best function for my analysis, and the covariates seemed to make sense, but I hit a wall when I got to the predictions. This is the link to my previous post:
https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/unmarked/15df3f9db05afa1a

Do you think I should actually be using distsamp()? I've actually ran the models with distsamp, and I do get reasonable predictions and CI, but the only covariate that comes up as affecting abundance is the one that was actually affecting availability in gdistsamp(). Am I missing something on how to interpret those predictions?

I really appreciate If you or others in the group could shed some light on this.

Thank you,

Fernanda.

messages.body_plain: If psi, p, gamma, epsilon were all modeled as ~1, there would be 4 parameters (and 4 starting values). With the monthly means parameterization as formulated here, you need 37: 1 for psi, and 12 for each of the other components of the model.

I ran this model using package unmarked:

mod3 <- pcountOpen(~sites, ~1, ~sites, ~sites, adults, K=50, dynamics="constant", se=FALSE)

Hi Jillian,

If you don't specify the 'newdata' argument, the predictions are for each site in your data. If you want predictions for particular sites or particular covariate values, you need to provide a data.frame to the 'newdata' argument. And if you want the covariate values to appear with the predictions, you need to set the argument 'appendData' to TRUE.

Richard

messages.body_plain:

Apologies if I'm just missing something obvious here, but I haven't been able to find my answer in old posts, so thanks in advance for any help. I'm looking at variables affecting bobwhite density in central Nebraska. I visited 48 points twice each. I'm using gdistsamp models.

The problem is that while I put "density" in for the model output argument, the model produces only abundance estimates (as do all my other models, and predict(), and coef() will not return density estimates when I ask for "state" estimates, only abundance estimates when I ask for "lambda".) Here is my umf and an example model that I'm running:

library(unmarked)
umf<-with(nobo_bin,{
  unmarkedFrameGDS(y=cbind(D50,D100,D150,D200,D250,D300),
                   siteCovs=data.frame(site_id, crp_type, habitat_type,

})
